ruled_out_vectors.title: SqrtPriceCalculator overflow → zero sqrtPrice bypass
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: Overflow in computeRatioX96 returns 0, bypassing pricing bounds in validateHandlerOrder
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96 returns 0 on uint160 overflow (line 51-52). However, validateHandlerOrder checks minSqrtPriceX96 which catches zero. Even if min=0 were set, CLOB fill price is computed independently of hook validation price — no economic impact.

ruled_out_vectors.title: Transient storage stale read across operations in same tx
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT persists across swaps, corrupting pricing validation
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: AMMStandardHook._validatePricingBounds writes to DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT in beforeSwap and reads+clears in afterSwap. The reentrancy guard (SWAP_GUARD_FLAG via nonReentrant) prevents a second swap from entering while the first is active, so stale reads cannot occur within a single tx.

ruled_out_vectors.title: Hook settings cache desync from registry
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: CreatorHookSettingsRegistry cache becomes stale, allowing bypassed hook enforcement
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: The registry intentionally allows cache staleness — documented in code comments. Hook settings are always validated at execution time via _enforceTokenHooks in the transfer handler, which reads current settings from AMM storage, not the registry cache. Cache is optimization only.

ruled_out_vectors.title: Reentrancy during hook fee distribution via _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS)
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers calls _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) which might clear reentrancy protection, allowing reentry during SafeERC20.safeTransfer
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags._setReentrancyFlags strips bits 0-1 from input flags, then preserves the current ENTERED bit (bit 1) via bitwise AND. NO_FLAGS=0 only clears custom flags (bits 2+), ENTERED bit remains set. Verified in source: `uint256 currentGuard = _getTstorish(REENTRANCY_GUARD_STORAGE) & ENTERED; _setTstorish(REENTRANCY_GUARD_STORAGE, currentGuard | flags);`

ruled_out_vectors.title: Re-entry via transfer handler callback during swap
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: Transfer handler ammHandleTransfer could be called directly to manipulate state mid-swap
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: CLOBTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer checks `msg.sender != AMM` and reverts. afterSwapRefund also requires msg.sender == AMM. No external caller can invoke handler callbacks.

ruled_out_vectors.title: Multi-swap transient storage overwrite in same tx
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: Second swap in same tx overwrites transient storage from first swap
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: nonReentrant modifier with SWAP_GUARD_FLAG prevents concurrent swaps. Each swap fully completes (including afterSwap hook and fee distribution) before the guard is released.

ruled_out_vectors.title: Native ETH refund manipulation via depositWrappedNativeAndRefundExcess
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: Low-level call for ETH refund could be exploited for reentrancy or value extraction
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: _depositWrappedNativeAndRefundExcess is called within nonReentrant context (ENTERED bit set). The low-level call sends excess ETH back to msg.sender, but reentrancy guard prevents any state manipulation. Amount is strictly `msg.value - requiredAmount`.

ruled_out_vectors.title: CLOB settlement reads stale reserves after swap
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: CLOB handler reads reserves before they are updated by swap, causing incorrect settlement
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: In _poolSwapByInput, reserves are updated (lines 1443-1451) before _finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse. The handler's ammHandleTransfer is called during finalization, after reserve update. _collectToken uses strict balance validation (before+amount == after).

theft_theses.title: Drain pool via reentrancy during hook fee distribution
theft_theses.reason: ENTERED bit preserved by _setReentrancyFlags — KV-4 proves protection holds

theft_theses.title: Extract value via zero-price CLOB fill
theft_theses.reason: Price validation catches zero — KV-1 proves no bypass path

theft_theses.title: Steal via direct handler callback invocation
theft_theses.reason: msg.sender == AMM check on all handler entry points — TM-1 proves access control holds

theft_theses.title: Manipulate settlement via transient storage corruption
theft_theses.reason: Reentrancy guard prevents concurrent operations — TM-2/KV-2 prove isolation

theft_theses.title: Extract ETH via refund manipulation
theft_theses.reason: Refund amount is strict (msg.value - required), reentrancy blocked — TM-3 proves safety

metadata.conclusion: Codebase is well-hardened against state desync attacks. Reentrancy guards correctly preserve ENTERED bit during flag manipulation. Transient storage isolation enforced by operation-level guards. Handler access control consistently applied. No exploitable findings.
